newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist firms launch defensive ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist firms launch defensive ad campaign.

text.p: Turkey's leading Islamist companies, accused by the secularist army of fostering Islamic fundamentalism, launched an advertising campaign on Monday to defend themselves.

"It is a very serious mistake to show us among the so-called 'companies helping fundamentalism' in newspapers and on TVs," read a full-page advertisement by Yimpas Holding, a flourishing food retailer, in many newspapers.

"Yimpas is a commercial company, committed to commercial activities. It is impossible for us to accept speculation about other activities," it said, referring to allegations that it was involved in supporting Islamist activism.

Turkey's powerful military, engaged in a war of attrition with the Islamist-led government, said last week in a set of strongly-worded briefings to senior civil servants and the media that "political Islam" was financially backed by "100 Islamist businessmen."

No company names were identified in the briefings, but newspaper reports said Kombassan, a construction, printing and machinery production company, and Yimpas, based in the conservative town of Yozgat, were among the leading Islamist firms.

Kombassan, run from Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's stronghold of Konya, caught the public eye when it bought a state tyre company after offering a higher-than-expected sum in a government sell-off shortly after Erbakan took office last June.
Nihat Abayhan, Kombassan's coordinator, rejected the army's "accusations" and said the company has been involved in "honest commerce since it was set up in 1989.
"We regret the army accusations. We are people who love our country and defend the national integrity of our country," he told Reuters.
"Such speculation does nothing but add to the existing political problems in Turkey," he said.
Erbakan is expected to hand over the premiership this week to Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller.

Turkey's capital market board (SPK) said at the weekend it started legal procedings against Kombassan, saying "the company attempted to raise its capital without being registered on the board's books."
Kombassan wants to raise its capital to 100 trillion lira ($685 million) from 39.5 trillion, which presently is the highest capital held by any Turkish company.
Its activities were highlighted last month when a company courier arriving at Ankara airport was caught, allegedly importing 1.7 million marks ($979,000) illegally from Germany.
Just a day earlier, a Yimpas board official, Kadir Sohbet, had been caught at the same airport allegedly trying to smuggle 24 kg of gold bullion into the country from Germany.
Prosecutions have been launched against both companies and inidividuals.
Abayhan said Kombassan is prepared to respond to the SPK claims, but the SPK's decision had not reached them yet.
"We have not done anything wrong in terms of capital market laws. We will speak when the law case comes before us," he said.
Asked if their business was affected after the military briefings, he said: "Just the opposite, we are doing better business now. It increased our popularity." He did not give details.
